questions.stem: Starch and cellulose are both made from glucose. Why do they have such different functions?

options.text: Starch is made from fructose while cellulose is made from glucose
Cellulose stores energy while starch provides structural support in cell walls
Starch is found only in animals while cellulose is found only in plants
Starch contains alpha-glucose with 1,4 and 1,6 glycosidic bonds forming a compact shape for energy storage, while cellulose contains beta-glucose with straight chains for structural support

questions.explanation: Although both are glucose polymers, starch uses alpha-glucose and forms coiled or branched structures ideal for compact energy storage. Cellulose uses beta-glucose, forming straight chains with hydrogen bonds between them, creating strong fibres suited for structural support in plant cell walls.
